The company behind ChatGPT just entered the chip business — and that changes the economics of AI for everyone.

OpenAI and Broadcom unveiled a custom inference chip this week, purpose-built to run large language models in production. Not training. Inference — the expensive, recurring cost of actually serving AI to users at scale.

Here is why this matters for business leaders: inference cost is the hidden tax on every AI deployment. Every chatbot answer, every agent decision, every AI-generated recommendation costs money at the hardware level. When those costs drop through custom silicon, products that were marginally viable become profitable, and capabilities that were too expensive to offer become standard.

This also signals a structural shift in the AI industry. The frontier is no longer just about building the smartest model. It is about who can deploy intelligence most efficiently. OpenAI is betting that controlling the full stack — from model to chip — is the path to dominance.

For enterprise leaders, the strategic question is whether your AI infrastructure is positioned for the cost curves ahead, or whether you are building on economics that will be outpaced within 18 months.
